speech.started.description: Runs when Cuebot starts reading a text out loud with its text-to-speech voice. Good for lighting up a talking avatar or showing who is being read.

fields.alias: The name of a voice (a "voice alias" from the Speech page). Empty means any voice.

variables.user: The viewer whose message is being read (empty for your own speech)
variables.source: Where the text came from, like chat or an action

speech.finished.description: Runs when Cuebot has finished reading a text out loud, or when it was skipped. Good for hiding a talking avatar again.

fields.alias: The name of a voice (a "voice alias" from the Speech page). Empty means any voice.

variables.alias: The voice name that was used
variables.user: The viewer whose message was read (empty for your own speech)
variables.duration: How long the speech took, in milliseconds
variables.skipped: True if it was skipped and not read

speech.stateChanged.description: Runs when speech is switched on or off, paused or resumed, or a VoiceGate profile changes. Good for showing a "speech paused" light on your stream.

variables.enabled: True if speech is switched on
variables.paused: True if the speech queue is paused
variables.eventsEnabled: True if event speech (reading follows, subs and so on) is on

voiceControl.command.description: Runs when you say one of your Voice Control commands into the microphone, like "scene gaming". You set up the spoken phrases on the Voice Control page.

fields.command: The name of a voice command from the Voice Control page. Several names can be separated by commas. Any means every command.

variables.voiceCommandName: The name of the command that was heard
variables.spokenTextInput: What you said after the command phrase (for commands that listen at the start)
variables.voiceCommandConfidencePercent: How sure Cuebot is that it heard right, 0 to 100

voiceControl.dictation.description: Runs for everything you say, once you finish a sentence, even when it is not a command. Good for turning speech into text on your stream.

fields.command: Only react when the sentence also contained this voice command (name from the Voice Control page, commas for several). Any means every sentence.

variables.spokenText: Everything that was heard in the sentence
variables.spokenTextConfidencePercent: How sure Cuebot is that it heard right, 0 to 100
variables.voiceCommandName: The name of the first command in the sentence (empty if none)
variables.voiceCommandCount: How many commands were in the sentence

audio.playSound.description: Plays one sound file on your computer, like an alert sound or a funny noise. It can wait until the sound is over or carry on straight away.

fields.file: The sound's full location on your computer, like C:\Sounds\airhorn.mp3. Works with .wav, .mp3, .ogg and .flac files.
fields.device: Which speakers or headphones to play on, picked from the list. Empty = your computer's normal sound output.
fields.volume: How loud, from 0 (silent) to 100 (full). The default is 100.
fields.wait: Tick to wait until the sound is over before the next step. Unticked, the next step starts right away.
fields.tag: Optional. A name you make up, so "Stop sounds" can stop all sounds with that name, like "alerts".
fields.useFileName: Tick to use the sound's file name (like "airhorn") as its tag, so "Stop sounds" can stop it by name.

variables.soundFile: The location of the sound that was played
variables.soundDuration: How long the sound lasts, in seconds
variables.soundDurationMs: How long the sound lasts, in milliseconds

audio.playSoundFromFolder.description: Plays one random sound from a folder on your computer. Add new files to the folder and they join in automatically. Great for a pile of different alert sounds.

fields.folder: The folder's full location on your computer, like C:\Sounds\Alerts.
fields.extensions: Which kinds of files to use, separated by commas, like "wav, mp3". Empty = every kind Cuebot can play.
fields.subfolders: Tick to also pick sounds from folders inside this folder.
fields.device: Which speakers or headphones to play on, picked from the list. Empty = your computer's normal sound output.
fields.volume: How loud, from 0 (silent) to 100 (full). The default is 100.
fields.wait: Tick to wait until the sound is over before the next step. Unticked, the next step starts right away.
fields.tag: Optional. A name you make up, so "Stop sounds" can stop all sounds with that name, like "alerts".
fields.useFileName: Tick to use the picked sound's file name (like "airhorn") as its tag, so "Stop sounds" can stop it by name.

variables.randomSoundFile: The location of the sound that was picked
variables.randomSoundFileName: The picked sound's file name, like airhorn.mp3
variables.soundDuration: How long the sound lasts, in seconds

audio.stopSounds.description: Stops sounds that Cuebot is playing right now. Good as a "shut up" button when an alert goes on too long.

fields.tag: Stop only sounds that have this tag. Empty = stop every sound.

speech.activateVoiceGate.description: Switches to another VoiceGate profile, or turns VoiceGate off. VoiceGate holds back new speech while your microphone hears you talking, so Cuebot does not talk over you.

fields.profile: The name of a VoiceGate profile from the Speech page. Type none to turn VoiceGate off.

variables.success: True if the profile was found and switched on

speech.clearQueue.description: Throws away everything waiting to be read out loud. The text being read right now finishes. Good when chat spams.

speech.pause.description: Pauses or resumes reading out loud. Texts wait in line while paused. Handy for a quiet moment on stream. This is the text-to-speech line, not the action queues on the Queues page.

fields.mode: Pause holds speech back. Resume lets it go on. Toggle switches to the opposite.

speech.setEvents.description: Switches reading of events out loud (follows, subs, tips and so on) on or off. Chat reading is not changed.

fields.mode: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches to the opposite.

speech.setEnabled.description: Switches all speech on or off. While off, Cuebot reads nothing out loud. Good for a "mute the bot" hotkey.

fields.mode: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches to the opposite.

speech.setUserVoice.description: Gives one viewer their own voice, so their chat messages sound different when read out loud. Leave the voice empty to give them the normal one back.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. The default %platform% means whoever started the action.
fields.user: The viewer's chat name. The default %user% means whoever started the action.
fields.userId: Optional. The viewer's id on their site. If empty, the name is used.
fields.alias: The name of the voice to use (a "voice alias" from the Speech page). Empty = go back to the normal voice.

speech.setAlias.description: Changes which voice is used for chat, for events, as the default, or for highlighted messages. Handy to switch voice for a funny part of the stream.

fields.target: Where the voice is used. Chat = viewer messages. Events = follows, subs and so on. Default = anything else. Highlight = highlighted messages.
fields.alias: The name of the voice to use (a "voice alias" from the Speech page). Empty = go back to the normal setting.

speech.speak.description: Reads a text out loud with a text-to-speech voice. Good for reading a viewer's message or a tip message. It can also save the speech as a file without playing.

fields.alias: The name of the voice to use (a "voice alias" from the Speech page). Empty = the default voice.
fields.text: What to say. You can use %variables%, like "%user% just followed".
fields.wait: Tick to wait until the speech is finished before the next step. Unticked, the next step starts right away.
fields.silent: Tick to only create the speech as an audio file without playing it out loud.
fields.badWordFilter: Tick to clean the text first: bad words, links and very long text are handled by your Speech page filters.
fields.filterProfile: Which set of filters to use, from the Speech page. Empty = the normal filters. Only used when filters are ticked.
fields.priority: Higher numbers are read first when several texts wait in line. 0 is normal.

variables.success: True if the text was read (false if it was skipped, for example by a filter)
variables.speechFile: Only after waiting or silent: the audio file that was made
variables.duration: Only after waiting or silent: how long the speech takes, in milliseconds

speech.next.description: Moves speech on by one text: stops the one being read, and if the queue is paused it lets exactly one waiting text start. Handy for stepping through a paused queue.

variables.success: True if a text was stopped or started

speech.skip.description: Stops the text being read right now. The next text in line (if any) is read after it. Good as a "skip" button for long messages.

speech.stopUser.description: Removes one viewer's waiting messages from the speech line and stops theirs if it is being read right now. Good when someone spams.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. The default %platform% means whoever started the action.
fields.user: The viewer's chat name. The default %user% means whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. The default %userId% means whoever started the action.

variables.stoppedCount: How many of their messages were stopped

voiceControl.setCommand.description: Changes the phrase of a Voice Control command, or makes a new command. Handy to change what you must say, for example one phrase per game.

fields.command: The name of a voice command from the Voice Control page, like "Switch scene".
fields.phrase: The words to listen for, like "scene gaming". You can use %variables%.
fields.location: Where the phrase can be in your sentence. Exact = it must be everything you say. Start = at the beginning. Anywhere = anywhere. Unchanged = keep the current setting.
fields.create: Tick to make the command if it does not exist yet. Unticked, a missing command gives an error.

variables.voiceCommandPhrase: The phrase it now listens for

voiceControl.setCommandState.description: Turns a Voice Control command on or off, or flips it. A turned-off command is ignored when you say it.

fields.command: The name of a voice command from the Voice Control page.
fields.state: Enabled turns it on. Disabled turns it off. Toggle switches to the opposite.

variables.voiceCommandEnabled: True if the command is on now

voiceControl.setInput.description: Chooses which microphone Voice Control listens to. Handy if you have several microphones. It works right away, also while listening.

fields.device: The microphone's name, picked from the list. Default = your computer's normal microphone.

voiceControl.setListening.description: Starts or stops Voice Control listening to your microphone. Good for a push-to-talk hotkey, so your commands are only heard when you want.

fields.state: Start begins listening. Stop ends it. Toggle switches to the opposite.

variables.voiceControlListening: True if Voice Control is listening now
